edits.after: At 3 Event Horizon and Dark Matter arrive — a spacing duel: dodge the cage and you win the trade, get clipped and you lose.

edits.after: Viktor

edits.before: Skill
edits.after: Viktor

edits.before: Chaos Storm online — your all-in answer and teamfight entry. In lane it's the kill: W-E-R on anyone who oversteps.
edits.after: His Primordial Burst needs the cage to land first — dodge Event Horizon and he has no ult angle; your W-E-R all-in is safer.

edits.before: Veigar
edits.after: Viktor

edits.before: Evolved late-game Viktor is a zone the enemy can't enter: W the choke, E the clump, and steer R through the retreat.
edits.after: Evolved Viktor fights from outside his cage window: W the choke, E the clump, and steer the storm through the retreat.

edits.before: - Veigar Event Horizon (Cage): matchup-defining — Only the cage EDGE stuns — hold position near the center or leave before it forms; never dash into the wall. It governs your forward steps. - W Gravity Field spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.
edits.after: - Veigar Event Horizon (Cage): 20s at rank 1, 14s at max — only the cage EDGE stuns; hold near the center or leave before it forms, never dash into the wall. - His R is 120/90/60s: once Primordial Burst is spent you have a full minute to bully. - Your W is 17s at rank 1 — never spend it on poke.

edits.before: E through the wave into his chest, Q-shield the response, empowered-auto, and walk — a full trade where his answer hit a shield.
edits.after: Drop Gravity Field on the path he must cross to cage you — the slow-then-stun turns his 725-range engage into a dead zone.

edits.before: Casting E at melee-adjacent range against a loaded engage — Viktor's cast times are an assassin's favorite metronome.
edits.after: Primordial Burst scales off your missing health — at half HP a stacked R after the cage deletes you before you can react.

edits.before: Veigar wins by landing Event Horizon (Cage), denying your pattern, and out-ranging your plan one polite trade at a time.
edits.after: Veigar wins by landing Event Horizon (Cage), chaining Dark Matter into Primordial Burst, and out-stacking you in a stalled lane.

edits.before: Through 4-5 your faster, longer Death Ray out-pokes his telegraphed spells.
edits.after: Through 4-5 your faster, longer Hextech Ray out-pokes his telegraphed spells.

edits.before: Your Death Ray out-ranges his Baleful Strike (Q) and doesn't telegraph like his Dark Matter (W), so you win the poke war at 3-5 as long as you sidestep his slow-landing meteor. Every time he walks up to Q a minion for stacks, clip him with E and back off.
edits.after: Your Hextech Ray out-ranges his Baleful Strike (Q) and doesn't telegraph like his Dark Matter (W), so you win the poke war at 3-5 as long as you sidestep his slow-landing meteor. Every time he walks up to Q a minion for stacks, clip him with E and back off.

edits.before: You scale more safely because you can fight from max range without stepping into his cage; evolved Death Ray plus Chaos Storm let you chip him and his team without ever committing into his one-shot window.
edits.after: You scale more safely because you can fight from max range without stepping into his cage; evolved Hextech Ray plus Chaos Storm let you chip him and his team without ever committing into his one-shot window.

edits.before: Levels 1-2 lean your way because Veigar is a pure scaling stacker with no early kill threat, so you farm freely and poke him whenever he reaches for a Baleful Strike stack. Keep the wave neutral so he has to walk up into your Death Ray angle to CS. Deny his passive stacks now — every minion he last-hits with Q feeds his late-game, so make each one cost him HP.
edits.after: Levels 1-2 lean your way because Veigar is a pure scaling stacker with no early kill threat, so you farm freely and poke him whenever he reaches for a Baleful Strike stack. Keep the wave neutral so he has to walk up into your Hextech Ray angle to CS. Deny his passive stacks now — every minion he last-hits with Q feeds his late-game, so make each one cost him HP.

edits.before: Through levels 3-5 you out-range and out-poke him: Death Ray flies faster and further than his Dark Matter, and you can sidestep the meteor's long cast time on reaction. The whole matchup hinges on his Event Horizon — never stand where he can cage you into a full combo. Shove the wave to pressure his stacking and keep chipping him so he can't safely reach for farm.
edits.after: Through levels 3-5 you out-range and out-poke him: Hextech Ray flies faster and further than his Dark Matter, and you can sidestep the meteor's long cast time on reaction. The whole matchup hinges on his Event Horizon — never stand where he can cage you into a full combo. Shove the wave to pressure his stacking and keep chipping him so he can't safely reach for farm.

edits.before: Around first item Veigar hits his one-shot spike if he's stacked, so the duel becomes skill: dodge the cage and you're fine, get caught and you die. Into two-plus items you scale more reliably because your range lets you fight without entering Event Horizon range at all — evolved Death Ray and Chaos Storm poke him and his team down while you stay outside his kill window.
